title: Benchmark workflow wall-clock reduction — kill dead sequencing, cut setup overhead, warm the Db2 boot
description:
Research note (2026-08-08, full write-up in `project-management/CI_BENCHMARK_PERFORMANCE.md`) on `.github/workflows/benchmarks.yml` as it stands after EPIC-24/CIB-1..7. That epic optimised for correctness and consolidation — DRY composite actions, container-only Db2, single-writer gh-pages, a `suite:` selector, a concurrency guard. All of that landed and none of it is being undone here. What it did not do is reduce wall clock: a `suite: all` dispatch still takes roughly 2–2.5 hours, and roughly 25 minutes per Db2 job of that is fixed setup overhead that buys nothing.

Critical path today is `db2-ready` → `max(benchmark-nightly, benchmark-scale)` → `consolidated-report`. Per-job overhead before a single benchmark executes:

| Phase | Cost | Paid by |
|---|---|---|
| `db2-ready` docker pull (~3 GB from icr.io) | 4–6 min | blocks 5 jobs |
| `pip install -e ".[dev,benchmark,...]"` | 4–8 min | 6 jobs |
| `setup-db2` — pull the *same* image again | 4–6 min | 5 jobs |
| `compose up --wait` (`start_period: 300s`, `interval: 30s`) | 5–10 min | 5 jobs |
| DDL readiness poll (flat 15 s sleep × up to 20) | 0–5 min | 5 jobs |

Findings, highest ROI first:

**A. `db2-ready` warms nothing.** Its stated purpose is to "confirm the image is accessible so that all downstream jobs can trust the image cache is warm on the runner pool." That premise is false on GitHub-hosted runners: every job gets a fresh VM with an empty Docker image store, so nothing pulled in `db2-ready` is visible to `benchmark`, `locust-isolation`, `locust-scale`, `benchmark-nightly`, or `benchmark-scale` — each re-pulls the full image inside `setup-db2` anyway. Meanwhile all five sit behind `needs: [db2-ready]`, so the pull is added to the critical path *and* duplicated. Note this contradicts EPIC-24 finding 6, which characterised the gate as a "fast-fail image-pull check" worth keeping; the fail-fast value is real but is not worth 4–6 min of serial latency on five jobs, and `setup-db2` already fails loudly on a bad image. The job's only genuine output is a constant string.

**B. Db2 boot is over-conservative.** `interval: 30s` means that once Db2 is ready you wait up to another 30 s to notice. Docker marks a container healthy on the first passing probe *including during `start_period`*, and probe failures during `start_period` don't count against `retries` — so a short interval paired with a long start period is strictly free. The DDL probe on top of it sleeps a flat 15 s and re-runs a full connect → CREATE TABLE → CREATE VECTOR INDEX → DROP cycle each attempt.

**C. `torch` installs in six jobs, three of which never use it.** `sentence-transformers>=5.6.1` in the `benchmark` extra pulls torch — a 527 MB manylinux x86_64 wheel, confirmed in `uv.lock`, ~2.5 GB unpacked. Every job requests `extras: benchmark,langchain,openai-agents,mcp`, including both Locust jobs and `consolidated-report`, which only reads JSON and writes HTML. The `actions/cache` on `~/.cache/pip` avoids the download but not the unpack. Compounding this: the repo commits a 1.6 MB `uv.lock` but CI installs with pip, keyed on `hashFiles('pyproject.toml')` with a loose `restore-keys` fallback that can silently restore a stale cache and misses transitive drift.

**D. `locust-scale` runs eight load steps strictly serially** — 22 minutes of pure load time on one runner, plus per-step ramp-up, on top of one Db2 boot.

**E. The 500k seed corpus is regenerated row-by-row every scale run.** Per the EPIC-25 audit, vectors cannot be parameter-bound on this Db2 version and are inlined as `CAST('{vec}' AS VECTOR(...))` literals, so every row is a distinct, unprepared, fully-logged statement. This is also the reason the `LOGFILSIZ 4096 LOGPRIMARY 30 LOGSECOND 64` expansion step exists.

**F. CIB-2's rejection of a custom Db2 image is worth reopening.** CIB-2 correctly identified why `jobs.<job>.services:` is blocked (GHA starts service containers before any step runs, so the host path bind-mounted to `/var/custom/01_create_testdb.sh` cannot be populated in time) and rejected a pre-baked image on maintenance/drift grounds. That was a reasonable call when the only benefit was unblocking `services:`. It now solves five things at once: removes the bind-mount, bakes TESTDB so the DDL poll disappears entirely, bakes the log config, pulls from GHCR in the same datacenter as the runner rather than from icr.io, and optionally carries the seeded corpus from (E).

Two items are genuine tradeoffs rather than clear wins and are gated behind spikes: the GHCR image (F) introduces a maintained artifact someone has to own, and matrixing the Locust sweeps (D) would inject inter-runner variance into BM-15's pool-size comparison — the exact axis being measured.

**Scope boundary:** this epic is about wall clock and CI cost only. The four-tier structure (EPIC-17), the consolidation and reporting architecture (EPIC-24), and the Db2 dialect seam (EPIC-25) are all out of scope. No benchmark's measurement duration is reduced for speed — `benchmark-nightly`'s 15-minute Locust ramp and the AGQ judge steps are intended measurement time and stay as they are.

**Caveat carried from the research note:** all timings are estimates from reading the workflow, not from measured run data. CIW-1 pulls real step durations first and re-ranks everything downstream; the Phase-1 stories are worth doing regardless because they're cheap and their reasoning doesn't depend on the estimates.

Target: `suite: all` critical path from ~2–2.5 h to ~50–70 min.
